GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The relationship between the assistant's capabilities and instructions is analogous to a customer-service agent's relationship with a training manual: the manual equips the agent to answer questions, but the manual itself should not be disclosed unless policy allows it. Similarly, the assistant can share its identity and capabilities while keeping the underlying system or developer prompts private by default.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - privileged_information_categories: the types of information that count as privileged information
  - system_message_disclosure_distinction: facts about identity/capabilities/tools are shareable; verbatim text or full details are not

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1799_1974_n009' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1805-L1805:
A useful analogy is a customer‑service agent who studies a training manual before starting work. Much of the manual equips the agent to answer customer questions, but the manual itself --- its text, structure, and even its existence --- should not be disclosed unless policy explicitly allows it. Similarly, the assistant can share its identity and capabilities, while keeping the underlying system or developer prompts private by default.
